paper: Stable Localized Conformal Prediction via Transduction

claims.statement: StCP/SLCP uses a conditional CDF estimator trained on labeled source-task data plus an empirical marginal distribution estimated from unlabeled target data, calibrated via a regularized optimization with parameter lambda.

must_hold: F_hat_S|X is fitted on labeled SOURCE data only (target labels never enter it)
the transductive term is computed from the m UNLABELED target covariates only
the optimised objective is exactly discrepancy + lambda * ||theta - theta_hat||^2 (Main/Tuner.py:202), verified arithmetically for every lambda and repeat
on the UNENFORCED path (direct tune_marginal calls, no check_order repair) ||theta - theta_hat||^2 shrinks from the smallest to the largest lambda in every repeat
refitting against covariates drawn from the SOURCE instead of the unlabeled TARGET sample moves the solution in every repeat
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: target labels reach the CDF estimator, the objective is not discrepancy + lambda*regulariser, the unenforced path does not shrink toward theta_hat, or the unlabeled target sample can be swapped for a source sample without changing the solution

claims.evidence_plan: Instrument the authors' own implementation on all five Table 1 datasets plus the LogAbs simulation; assert the data-flow invariants above by construction-tracing, and measure the lambda=0 identity and the lambda->infinity limit numerically.
claims.non_circularity_note: Main/SLCP.py:8 `check_order` re-trains any lambda whose (discrepancy, delta) pair breaks the Pareto ordering, looping up to 3*|Lambda| times. Monotonicity read off `tune_lbd_list` output is therefore imposed by the implementation and is NOT admissible evidence. Claim 1 is adjudicated only on the path measured by calling `tune_marginal` directly per lambda on independent copies.
claims.negative_control: Refit the transductive term against covariates drawn from the SOURCE distribution. The fitted solution must move; if it does not, the transduction is inert and the check is not discriminating.
claims.withdrawn_check: An earlier revision compared SLCP.q against the conformal score quantile of F_hat_S^0 and measured a gap of ~29 median score spacings. That comparison was invalid: SLCP.q is a PROBABILITY level, passed as the `q` argument of Generator.quantile (Main/SLCP.py:90), not a score threshold. The check is withdrawn rather than reinterpreted, and no verdict was ever derived from it.

claims.statement: |P(Y in C_St) - (1-alpha)| <= C * min(eps + lambda^{1/2} + n^{-1}, delta_S + lambda^{-1/2} + n^{-1}).
claims.quantifier_structure: exists C>0 such that for all lambda; C is unspecified

must_hold: empirical marginal coverage stays close to 1-alpha across the paper's full lambda grid on the paper's own settings
the measured coverage deviation is bounded by the theorem's envelope for SOME finite constant C fitted on held-out lambda values, i.e. the envelope shape (not merely its level) matches
the two-regime structure is visible: deviation is controlled by eps at small lambda and by delta_S at large lambda

the fitted envelope explains the lambda-to-deviation relationship better than chance: refitting after permuting the deviations across lambda must reproduce the held-out fit no more than 5% of the time
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: coverage deviation grows without bound in lambda, or no finite C reproduces the min(.,.) envelope on held-out lambda

claims.non_circularity_note: C must be fitted on a disjoint subset of the lambda grid from the one used to test the envelope, otherwise the check is a tautology.
claims.negative_control: Replace the transductive alignment with the uncorrected direct plug-in (DP), whose coverage the paper says can deviate severely; the envelope check must FAIL for DP.
claims.vacuity_guard: min(eps + sqrt(lambda) + 1/n, delta_S + 1/sqrt(lambda) + 1/n) has three free parameters and can absorb many curves, so a good held-out fit alone is weak evidence. The permutation control is what makes the check non-vacuous: it asks whether the SHAPE carries information at all, and a curve that fits equally well under a random lambda pairing has demonstrated nothing about Theorem 4.2.
claims.scoping_note: Requiring in-band coverage at EVERY lambda would be stricter than the theorem, which bounds the deviation by an unspecified constant rather than pinning it inside the table-annotation band. The check therefore requires robustness over most of the grid (>=80% of lambda values in band on average) plus the envelope and permutation tests, and reports the per-setting in-band fraction rather than silently thresholding it.

claims.statement: Standard conformal set-size variance is O(n^{-1}); StCP achieves O(m^{-1} + {n(1+lambda)^2}^{-1}), giving stability gains when m >> n.

must_hold: log-log regression of base set-size variance on n over n in {30,100,500} at m=500 has slope statistically consistent with -1
StCP variance decreases monotonically in lambda over the region where marginal coverage remains valid
at fixed n, StCP variance decreases as m increases over m in {30,100,500}, and the m-dependence flattens once m >> n
a two-term fit a/m + b/(n(1+lambda)^2) explains the measured StCP variance surface better than a pure 1/n law
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: the base slope is inconsistent with -1, or StCP variance fails to decrease in lambda, or the m>>n regime shows no gain

claims.non_circularity_note: n is swept over values the paper itself uses (30/100/500) and the slope is fitted, never assumed. The lambda- and m-monotonicity checks read set-size standard deviations, which `check_order` does not touch -- unlike the discrepancy/delta ordering used in Claim 1.
claims.negative_control: The oracle baseline, which augments calibration with real labels, must show the 1/n law with a smaller constant but NOT the m-driven term.
claims.vacuity_guard: The log-log slope's interval must be BOOTSTRAPPED from the repeats, not derived from an asymptotic formula. An earlier revision perturbed the point estimate by exp(N(0,1/sqrt(2*49))) -- the asymptotic s.e. of a log-variance from 50 draws -- which assumes the sampling distribution instead of measuring it and would report a tight interval even if the repeats disagreed. Only three values of n are available, so the interval is wide by construction and must be reported, not hidden.

claims.anchor: Table 1, Section 5.1, Appendix C.1 and C.3
claims.statement: On real data across five datasets, StCP/SLCP reduces prediction-set-size standard deviation by 20-48% when built on GLCP and by 6-29% when built on CQR, while maintaining marginal coverage near the nominal 90% level.

machine_checkable_contract.improvement_formula: (a_ref - a_1) / (a_ref - a_0) * 100, a_ref = min Std over base/SDCP/PPI with in-range marginal coverage, a_0 = oracle Std
must_hold: all five datasets run to completion on the authors' own entry scripts and data
each reproduced oracle-adjusted percentage has a bootstrap CI covering the published value
marginal coverage of `ours` is inside the authors' real-data annotation band on every cell
every reproduced GLCP cell lies within 20-48% and every CQR cell within 6-29%, allowing 0.5 point of slack for the claim's integer endpoints
machine_checkable_contract.adjudication: The claim's stated GLCP band 20-48% is checked against every reproduced cell, including TISSUE, whose published value is 13.5% and therefore already falls outside the stated band. The verdict must state whether the band holds as written, holds only for a subset, or is contradicted.
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: any reproduced cell falls outside the claimed band by more than the endpoint rounding slack

claims.negative_control: The direct plug-in (DP) variant must show the severe upward marginal-coverage deviation the paper reports, confirming the alignment step is what buys validity.
claims.adjudication: Cell-by-cell agreement with the printed table is a PRECONDITION, not a check that can be traded off: if the reproduction does not match Table 1 the verdict is BLOCKED, because a disagreeing reproduction cannot convict the paper of anything. Only once agreement holds does a band violation become a falsification.
claims.paper_internal_finding: The claimed bands do not cover the paper's own Table 1. GLCP spans 13.5-48.4% against a claimed 20-48%. STAR/GLCP (48.4) and BIO/CQR (29.3) are within half a point of the stated integer endpoints and are treated as rounding. TISSUE/GLCP at 13.5% is 6.5 points below the claimed floor and cannot be explained by rounding. This holds independently of the reproduction.
claims.vacuity_guard: The 20-48% and 6-29% bands are wide, so 'the reproduction landed in the band' is weak on its own. The binding evidence is per-cell agreement with the published value inside a bootstrap CI over the 50 repeats, which a wide band cannot absorb.

claims.statement: On synthetic data the largest stability gains occur at n=30, with standard deviation reductions of 31.2% (GLCP-based) and 16.3% (CQR-based).

machine_checkable_contract.dgp: LogAbs, d=5, mu_s=0, mu_t=1_d/(2 sqrt d), Y'=(3/d) sum X'_j + eps', Y=(2/d) sum X_j + eps, sigma(x;gamma)=sqrt(gamma) * sum_j log(1+|x_j|)/sqrt(d), gamma_s=1.2, gamma_t=1.0
must_hold: the reproduced n=30 GLCP std reduction has a bootstrap CI covering the published 31.2%
the reproduced n=30 CQR std reduction has a bootstrap CI covering the published 16.3%
the no-shift control (r=0, gamma_s=gamma_t) reduces the gain for BOTH base methods
no rival calibration size is strictly larger than n=30 at 95% for the GLCP row
machine_checkable_contract.adjudication: The published CQR column is 16.3 / 16.7 / 6.3 for n = 30 / 100 / 500, so the 'largest gains at n=30' wording is exactly true for GLCP but off by 0.4 points for CQR. The verdict must state this rather than smooth it over.
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: reproduced n=30 reductions differ from 31.2% / 16.3% by more than Monte-Carlo error

claims.negative_control: Re-run with the covariate and noise shift removed (r=0, gamma_s=gamma_t), which removes the reason transductive calibration should help. The gain must shrink. This control is BINDING: an earlier revision computed it but omitted it from the verdict, so it could not fail anything.
claims.vacuity_guard: An ordering the 50 repeats cannot resolve is NOT a falsification. The published GLCP argmax is a fact about the table with no sampling error, so the reproduction can only contradict it; the check fails only when a rival n is strictly larger at 95%, never when the interval merely straddles zero.
claims.paper_internal_inconsistency: The claim states the largest gains occur at n=30, but the paper's own Table 2 CQR row gives 16.7% at n=100 against 16.3% at n=30. The qualifier therefore fails for CQR on the paper's own numbers, independent of any reproduction. The margin is 0.4 points, so the reproduction reports a bootstrap CI on the n=30 minus rival difference rather than asserting the ordering either way.

claims.statement: The data-driven lambda selection rule maintains empirical coverage within [1-alpha-alpha_tol, 1-alpha+alpha_tol+(n+1)^{-1}).
claims.band_is_not_the_table_annotation_band: Table 1/2 mark coverage with [1-alpha-0.01, 1-alpha+1/(n+1)] = [0.89, 0.932258]; Theorem 4.7's guarantee band is the wider [0.88, 0.952258).
claims.quantifier_structure: universally quantified over exchangeable score sequences

must_hold: ours-sel marginal coverage lies in the predicted band on every one of the five real datasets and every simulation setting, for both base types
the selected lambda_hat equals max of the feasible set on every repeat (rule implemented as stated)
the band is checked two-sided, and the observed coverage is reported with a Monte-Carlo interval
machine_checkable_contract.fails_if: coverage falls outside the band at any assumption-satisfying setting

claims.vacuity_guard: The band is ~7.2 points wide, so an in-band observation is weak on its own: the claim stays BLOCKED unless the non-exchangeable control leaves the band. Symmetrically, a point estimate just outside the band is NOT a falsification -- coverage is estimated from finitely many repeats, so each setting carries a bootstrap interval and only a setting whose entire interval lies outside counts against Theorem 4.7.
claims.negative_control: Non-exchangeable calibration (target calibration scores drawn from the shifted source distribution) must push ours-sel coverage outside [0.88, 0.952258).
